findings.text: Group descriptor holds a subgroup label in name plus alternative regular visibility hooks where one form accepts a mutable entry and the other accepts an immutable entry, together with a binary visibility hook and a binary size hook. Regular members arrive through either a mutable list member or an immutable list member, while binary members arrive from a separate immutable list member. Regular hooks are known as is_visible and is_visible_const with binary visibility as is_bin_visible and binary sizing as bin_size, while regular lists appear as attrs and attrs_const with binary list as bin_attrs.
Preallocation marker uses octal digits one followed by four zeros and group invisible marker uses octal digits two followed by four zeros.

Visibility helper for a named group reports the group invisible marker when asked about the first index while the group level predicate for that name denies visibility, and otherwise delegates to the per entry visibility routine for that name or to the entry mode for the simple forms. Binary and regular forms follow the same first index rule, and a constructor builds the helper name from the group name.

Regular entry constructors associate a stringified name with a validated mode and optional display and update callbacks. Variants cover preallocated entries and read only entries using a fixed read mode or a caller mode with an implied display callback plus write only entries with an implied update callback and read write entries with implied callbacks, plus a terminator with an empty name. Display callback is known as show and update callback as store.

Lock dependency handling for regular entries has two builds where one build records an ignore request alongside name and mode with callbacks and the other build behaves identically to the ordinary constructor.

Group list helpers create a singleton group from a same named list with automatic handling of mutable versus immutable lists, and also create an empty terminated list containing that singleton. A binary variant builds the singleton from a binary list instead.

Binary descriptor starts from a base member named attr and adds an extent member named size plus an opaque member named private. File mapping indirection is provided by a dedicated hook. Data access uses separate read and write hooks with repositioning through a seek hook and address mapping through a map hook, each receiving file and owning object context together with the descriptor itself. Hooks are known as f_mapping and read plus write with llseek and mmap.
Binary initialization delegates to the generic initializer applied to the embedded base member.

Binary constructors bind a stringified name with a mode plus read and write callbacks and an extent. Variants cover read only and write only plus read write with conventional modes and implied callback names, administrative read only and read write with owner only modes, simple read only forms using a shared read routine with zero extent, and an empty terminator. Uppercase forms also declare a persistent instance with a prefixed identifier.
File operations for regular entries expose a display hook and an update hook, each receiving the owning object and the entry plus a buffer with length for updates. Hooks are known as show and store.

When the feature is disabled the management helpers for directories and mount points plus files and links with groups and ownership changes either have no effect or report success, while self removal reports a negative answer and active protection break reports an empty handle. Notification and removal helpers have no effect and initialization reports success, while emit helpers and simple binary read report no bytes.

Enabled path helpers forward namespace activation and notification plus reference lookup and reference counting to the underlying hierarchical store, and the plain link rename forwards to the namespace aware form with no namespace.

Mode validation requires a value between zero and triple seven octal inclusive, requires readability not to increase from owner toward group toward other, requires writability not to increase from owner toward group, and forbids writability for other.
Extended attribute argument structure initial published size is sixteen, and latest size equals that initial size.

Extended attribute handler carries a name string and a prefix string plus private flags. Listing support is optional, while retrieval and modification use dedicated hooks with transaction context including mount mapping and directory plus inode with names and buffers and lengths and flags. Members are known as name and prefix with flags, and hooks as list and get with set.
Listing eligibility holds when a handler exists and either it provides no list hook or its list hook approves the given directory entry.
Simple name value carrier holds a name pointer in name plus a payload pointer in value with its length in value_len.

Simple extended attribute cache holds a hash table pointer. Each entry links hash and list plus parent state with deferred reclamation, then a name pointer and a size with a trailing payload sized by that size. Limits track current user entry count and current total payload bytes. Count is known as nr_xattrs and total as xattr_size with table as ht and entry payload as value.
Simple store caps user entries at one hundred twenty eight and total payload at one hundred twenty eight kibibytes.
Initial open file limit is one thousand twenty four and hard limit is four thousand ninety six. Block size shift is ten giving a block size of one thousand twenty four.

Integrity checks use bit zero for guard and bit one for reference with bit two for application, with a combined valid mask. Seek origins are zero for start and one for current with two for end and three for data plus four for hole with maximum equal to hole. Rename flags use bit zero for no replace and bit one for exchange with bit two for whiteout.
Process filesystem root inode number is one.
Clone range carries source descriptor with source offset and length plus destination offset. Trim range carries start and length with minimum length.
Filesystem identifier pairs a length with sixteen identifier bytes. Filesystem sysfs path pairs a length with a one hundred twenty eight byte name.

Logical block metadata capability uses bit zero for integrity and bit one for reference tag. Checksum types are zero for none and one for internet checksum with two for T10DIF CRC sixteen and four for NVME CRC sixty four. Version zero size is sixteen.
Capability descriptor starts with flags and interval then size and opaque tag size plus offset, followed by protection tuple size and offset with guard type and tag extents plus padding.
Deduplication comparison reports zero for same and one for differs.

Per destination deduplication status holds destination descriptor and offset with deduplicated byte count plus a signed status and a reserved word. The enclosing request holds source offset and length with destination count plus reserved words and a trailing array of per destination entries.
Open file statistics hold total and free plus maximum counts. Inode statistics hold total and unused counts with five spare words for compatibility.
Compiled default maximum open files is eight thousand one hundred ninety two.

Extended inode attributes carry flags and extent size with nextent count plus project identifier and copy on write extent size, with an older form using thirty two bit flags and eight pad bytes and a newer form using sixty four bit flags without padding.
Newer attribute structure version zero size is twenty four and latest equals that.
Callers must leave reserved words cleared in deduplication requests and must inspect per destination status for error versus same versus differs rather than assuming uniform success.
Entry modes must preserve readability ordering from owner to group to other and writability ordering from owner to group while keeping other non writable, otherwise build time validation fails.
